orders.title: Orders
orders.text: Buyers' orders by ship date: pieces by size and colour, value, and what each needs from the store.
orders.made: Order {number} made. Fill in the pieces by size and colour.
orders.dialog_text: Pick the style (its buyer comes with it). The pieces by size and colour come next, on the order.
orders.no_styles: Make a style first: an order is always for a style.
orders.empty_text: A buyer's order (PO) for a style shows here with its ship date and pieces.
orders.not_found: That order does not exist here.

steps.confirm_text: The buyer's order is firm. Pieces can still change while it is confirmed (buyers amend).
steps.start_text: From now on its pieces and price no longer change.
steps.cancel_text: The order stays on the list as cancelled, with your reason.

sheet.title: Pieces by size and colour
sheet.text_open: Type the pieces in each cell; totals add up as you type. Save when done.

needs.title: Materials needed
needs.text: From the style's bill of materials, with wastage, against what all the company's stores hold now.
needs.empty_text: Add the style's bill of materials and the pieces of the order.

styles.title: Styles and BOM
styles.text: Each buyer's styles: sizes, colours and what one piece or dozen is made of.
styles.dialog_text: The buyer comes from CRM; you can add a new one here.
styles.empty_text: Add a buyer's style with its sizes and colours, then its bill of materials.
styles.not_found: That style does not exist here.

bom.title: Bill of materials
bom.text: What it takes {per}, with wastage. A line can be for one size or colour only.
bom.empty_text: Add fabric, thread, buttons, labels, packing… each an Inventory item.

buyers.add_text: Kept in CRM as an organization tagged "buyer", with its contacts, calls and deals.
buyers.name: Buyer's name

fields_.list_hint: In order, with a comma between.
fields_.finished_item_hint: Finished pieces of this style go into the store as this Inventory item (sizes and colours stay here).

fields.title: Own fields
fields.text: Fields your factory adds to orders and styles (season, GSM, fabric composition…). Key and kind stay once made; a field is switched off, never removed.
fields.empty_order: Add what your orders need beyond the usual: season, payment terms, port…
fields.empty_style: Add what your styles need: GSM, fabric composition, wash…
fields.label: Name
fields.key_hint: Lower case letters, digits and _ (made from the English name if left empty).

conflict: Someone changed this a moment ago. It is fresh now; make your change again.

issues.title: Given to the floor and taken back
issues.text: Every issue and return for this order, at what the store valued it.
issues.give_text: Stock leaves the store at its cost and counts as work in progress.
issues.back_text: What comes back goes into the store again at its share of what it cost.
issues.nothing_needed: This order needs no materials yet: add the style's bill of materials.
issues.nothing_out: Nothing of this order is on the floor.
issues.no_store: There is no store in use. Add one in Inventory first.
issues.over_text: These go above what the bill of materials works out:
issues.confirm_first: Materials go to the floor once the order is confirmed.
issues.empty_text: Give materials once the order is confirmed.

cutting.title: Cutting
cutting.new_text: Type the pieces cut in this lay. At most {percent}% above the order per size and colour.
cutting.too_many: Too many for: {cells}. Keep them to what is left (with the allowance).
cutting.empty_text: Cutting starts production: the first lay puts a confirmed order into production.
cutting.confirm_first: Confirm the order first; then lays can be cut.
cutting.void_text: Its pieces stop counting and can be cut again. The lay stays in the list.

sewing.title: From cutting to the store
sewing.text: Each size and colour: cut, sewn good, rejected, and in the store as finished goods.
sewing.take_title: Finished goods of {number} into the store
sewing.take_text: Good pieces sewn and not in the store yet. They come in at their share of the work in progress.
sewing.fill_ready: Fill in all that is ready
sewing.too_many: More than is sewn and ready for: {cells}.
sewing.last_hint: Takes all the work in progress left into the cost, so nothing stays behind.
sewing.no_item: Choose the style's finished item first (Styles → edit).
sewing.empty_text: Good pieces go into the store once sewn.

output.title: Line output
output.text: What each sewing line makes, every hour. Works without a network too.
output.too_many: More than was cut and is still to sew.
output.nothing_cut: Nothing of this order is cut yet.
output.kept_offline: No network: kept on this phone, it goes when the network is back.
output.offline_off: No network, and Offline mode is not on for this phone. Try again when the network is back.
output.offline_note: No network: lines and orders as this phone last kept them. What you save goes later.
output.empty_text: Entries appear here as lines write them.
output.no_lines_text: Add the factory's lines in Settings → Sewing lines.
output.no_orders_text: An order goes into production when its first lay is cut.
output.void_text: Its pieces stop counting and can be written again. The entry stays in the list.
output.no_smv: This style has no operation bulletin yet: no target.
output.people_hint: Write who works on the line today to see the hour's target and efficiency.

lines.title: Sewing lines
lines.text: The factory's lines: output is written for each of them.
lines.dialog_text: A short code (L-01) and a name. A line no longer used is switched off; its output stays.
lines.name: Name
lines.in_use_hint: Off: no new output for it; what it made stays.
lines.empty_text: Add a line for each group of machines that sews together.

operations.title: Operation bulletin
operations.text: Each sewing job with its standard minutes (SMV) and piece rate. This style: {smv} minutes a piece.
operations.name: Operation
operations.rates_need_manager: Only a factory manager can set or change piece rates. Keep the rates as they were, or ask a manager.
operations.empty_text: Add the style's sewing jobs and their minutes: the line's target and efficiency come from them.

qc.title: Quality checks
qc.text: End-line checks of each line, and final inspections of orders before they ship.
qc.lot_hint: Sample and the most defects accepted come from the AQL {aql} table.
qc.sample: Check {sample} pieces: at most {accept} defects to pass.
qc.final_fail: Final inspection failed: re-check after rework.
qc.empty_text: Checks appear here as inspectors save them.
qc.void_text: It stops counting; a voided final inspection no longer lets the order ship.

quality.no_finals_text: Do it when the order is packed, before it ships.
quality.can_ship: The last final inspection passed: the order can ship.
quality.needs_final: The order ships only after a passed final inspection.

defects.title: Kinds of defect
defects.text: What QC counts at end-line checks and final inspections.
defects.dialog_text: A short code and a name in each language.
defects.name: Name
defects.in_use_hint: Off: not counted any more; past counts keep it.

tickets.title: Piece tickets
tickets.text: What each operator did: pieces of an operation at its rate. Payroll adds it to the month's pay.
tickets.nobody: No one found working here that day.
tickets.empty_text: Tickets appear here as they are written.
tickets.locked: This month's payroll is approved: its tickets no longer change.
tickets.no_hrm_text: Piece tickets are for HRM's employees. Turn HRM on to pay piece rates.
tickets.void_text: It stops paying. It stays in the list.

shipments.title: Shipments
shipments.none_ready: Nothing in the store to ship yet: take finished goods in first.
shipments.new_text: The packing list is written on the shipment's page next.
shipments.made: Shipment {number} made. Write its packing list.
shipments.empty_text: Finished goods in the store can be shipped in one or more shipments.
shipments.rate_hint: The exchange rate for the invoice in the books.
shipments.last_label: This is the order's last shipment
shipments.last_hint: When it ships, the order is marked shipped.
shipments.totals: {cartons} cartons · {pieces} pcs · net {net} kg · gross {gross} kg · {cbm} CBM
shipments.no_cartons_text: Add a row for each run of cartons packed the same.
shipments.ship_text: {pieces} pieces leave the store; the shipment no longer changes.
shipments.shipped_invoice: Shipped. A draft invoice to the buyer is waiting in Accounting.
shipments.shipped_note: Shipped: the goods left the store.
shipments.shipped_note_invoice: Shipped: the goods left the store, and a draft invoice to the buyer waits in Accounting for an accountant to post.
shipments.not_found: That shipment does not exist here.

lcs.title: Letters of credit
lcs.text: Buyers' L/Cs: what each has paid for, the last day to ship and the expiry.
lcs.new_text: Its orders are ticked on the L/C's page next.
lcs.made: L/C saved. Tick the orders it pays for.
lcs.empty_text: Buyers who pay by L/C: keep each one here to ship within its terms.
lcs.usage_text: {left} left of {ceiling} with the tolerance · drafts {drafts}
lcs.orders_text: The buyer's orders in the L/C's currency; an order goes under one L/C.
lcs.no_orders: The buyer has no order in this currency
lcs.no_shipments: No shipment under this L/C yet
lcs.close_text: No more shipments go under it. Its papers and history stay.
lcs.not_found: That L/C does not exist here.
lcs.discrepancy_title: The L/C's terms are not kept
lcs.discrepancy_text: Banks often accept these for a fee. Ship anyway?

discrepancies.lc_late: Shipped after the last day to ship
discrepancies.lc_over: More than the L/C's amount with its tolerance
discrepancies.lc_partial: A part shipment, which the L/C does not allow

paper.at_sight: At sight of this FIRST bill of exchange (SECOND of the same tenor and date being unpaid)
paper.at_days: At {days} days after sight of this FIRST bill of exchange (SECOND of the same tenor and date being unpaid)
paper.bill_body: pay to the order of {bank} the sum of {amount}, value received, drawn under L/C no. {lc} dated {date} issued by {issuer}.
paper.certificate_body: We hereby certify that the goods under commercial invoice no. {invoice} have been shipped as per L/C no. {lc} dated {date}, and that one full set of non-negotiable documents has been sent to {buyer}.
paper.checklist_intro: Documents presented under L/C no. {lc} to {bank}:
